page: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a dedicated GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 threads operating at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The system is equipped with 84 GB of system memory, providing 5.25 GB per core, and includes 400 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The defining hardware feature of this instance is the inclusion of three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs based on the Turing architecture. Each GPU provides 16 GiB of VRAM, yielding a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. This hardware configuration is highly optimized for parallel processing tasks, particularly large language model (LLM) inference. Benchmark data shows top-tier performance in LLM prompt processing and text generation across small, medium, and large models, with the 70B model achieving 220.48 tokens per second for prompt processing and 7.46 tokens per second for text generation.

General CPU and memory benchmarks place the instance in the average tier. Single-core and multi-core performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, show middle-tier results. While the Passmark memory score is strong, large-block memory write speeds and single-threaded gzip compression are weaker relative to other resources. This indicates a tradeoff where the instance delivers exceptional GPU-bound performance but standard performance for CPU-only sequential tasks.

Given its hardware profile, the rtx5000-84 offers high resource density for GPU-intensive workloads. It is highly suited for LLM inference, ray tracing, image processing, and parallelized scientific computing. The combination of dedicated Intel Xeon cores and triple NVIDIA GPUs makes it a robust platform for machine learning deployments and graphics-heavy rendering tasks.

While CPU-bound sequential tasks and large-block memory writes show average to weak performance, the instance excels in GPU-intensive operations.
